title: Inverse Greedy — exponential-clock uniformity of maximal independent sets
headline: A Lean-verified classification of exact random-greedy uniformity for graphs on at most five vertices, with one exceptional path.
description: This project asks whether strictly positive, finite rates for independent exponential vertex clocks can make a random greedy algorithm uniform over a graph's inclusion-maximal independent sets. Its complete Lean 4-verified classification for graphs on at most five vertices shows that every such graph is uniformisable except the five-vertex path $P_5$, up to whole-graph isomorphism; a strict probability minor obstructs $P_5$. The theorem has a Palomar registration and an arXiv preprint, but graphs of larger order remain unclassified and the connected six-vertex computational atlas contains unresolved cases.
summary: The inverse problem permits unequal arrival rates, unlike the equal-rate random-priority model. Exact constructive witnesses, isomorphism reduction and a positive algebraic obstruction yield the five-vertex classification, with an independent-exponential-clock law formalised in Lean 4. A separate connected six-vertex atlas reports 90 EGU, 8 non-EGU and 45 unresolved graph classes; these partial computations are not a six-vertex theorem. The preprint has not undergone journal peer review, and the targeted prior-art audit is not an unconditional novelty certificate.
verification: The full at-most-five-vertex iff is proved as `PalomarEGU.graphs_le_five_iff` using the actual independent exponential-clock law. Lean, NanoDa and con-ron kernel checks and Palomar Comparator checks passed for the submitted proof. Palomar v1 records the preserved source commit `f4079bc46017e0b393f3678a0ab710eab1490116` and status 'registered'; the Lean axioms reported are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. This is formal proof verification, not a novelty or peer-review certificate.
attribution: John Fairfax-Ball is the named author and research lead. The project's inverse rate-design classification, exact graph witnesses and formal proof were developed under human direction with substantial AI assistance, including OpenAI GPT-6 for mathematical exploration, code, Lean formalisation, checking, figures and manuscript preparation. Earlier random sequential adsorption and random greedy independent-set literature is separately credited.
